'''Veronika Meduna''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|CF}} is a scientist, science journalist and broadcaster who was the founding [[New Zealand]] editor of ''[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]''.

== Early life ==
Meduna was born in [[Czechoslovakia]] and spent her childhood there before moving with her family to [[Germany]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2017}}

== Career ==
Meduna trained and worked as a [[microbiologist]] before moving into science journalism. She is best known as the long-serving producer and presenter of the ''Our Changing World'' science show on [[Radio New Zealand]], producing and presenting hundreds of episodes of the show.

=== Science ===
Between 1988 and 1990, she was a research assistant at the [[University of Konstanz]] in the "Microbial Ecology Working Group" and subsequently, until 1992, as a scientist at the Konstanz-based Bio System GmbH. There, she dealt with soil microbiology, investigated, among other things, the potential of earth microbes for the purification of contaminated soil and developed a technique for the biological removal of pollutants. In 1992, Meduna held two positions as a research associate: On the one hand, she was involved in the extraction and refining of algentoxins at the [[University of Bremen]] (now known as the Center for Environmental Research and Sustainable Technologies) and also contributed to a study that was to assess the environmental factors responsible for the planting of the algal bloom. In addition, she participated in the Department of Zoology, Wildlife Management at the [[University of Otago]], on a comprehensive observation of New Zealand seabirds on the Otago Peninsula.

=== Journalism ===
She joined Radio New Zealand in 1999 as a science reporter covering the Royal Commission on Genetic Modification before hosting ''Our Changing World''. Alongside her broadcast career, Meduna has been an award winning science writer, contributing to publications such as the [[New Zealand Listener]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.noted.co.nz/archive/listener-nz-2012/science-on-ice-by-veronika-meduna-review/?wpmp_switcher=mobile|title=Science on Ice by Veronika Meduna – review - The Listener|last=Noted|website=Noted|language=en|access-date=2017-08-06}}</ref> [[New Zealand Geographic]] and [[New Scientist]].

She left RNZ in 2016<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencemediacentre.co.nz/2016/07/29/paying-tribute-to-a-science-reporting-star/|title=Paying tribute to a science reporting star|date=2016-07-29|access-date=2017-08-06}}</ref> as part of a major restructure at the broadcaster and worked as a freelance journalist before joining ''The Conversation'' in May 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/ED1706/S00069/ithe-conversationi-appoints-new-zealand-editor-veronika.htm|title='The Conversation' Website Appoints NZ Editor Veronika Meduna |publisher= Scoop News|access-date=2017-08-06}}</ref>

She spent time at [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] as a Chevening David Low Fellow.<ref>{{cite web|title=Veronika Meduna|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/national/presenters/veronika-meduna|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |accessdate=7 August 2017|language=en-nz}}</ref>

Meduna won the [[Elsie Locke Award for Non-Fiction]] at the 2009 LIANZA awards and was shortlisted for the 2013 Royal Society of New Zealand Science Book Prize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.press.auckland.ac.nz/en/browse-books/all-books/books-2012/Science-on-Ice-Discovering-the-Secrets-of-Antarctica.html|title=Science on Ice: Discovering the Secrets of Antarctica - The University of Auckland|website=www.press.auckland.ac.nz|access-date=2017-08-06}}</ref> In 2021, Meduna was awarded a [[Churchill Fellowship]] to travel to Micronesia, Melanesia and Australia, to carry out research for a book on the settlement of the Pacific.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.communitymatters.govt.nz/winston-churchill-memorial-trust-2/winston-churchill-memorial-trust-2021-fellowships-and-their-research-reports/ |title=Winston Churchill Memorial Trust 2021 fellowships and their research reports |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She lives and works in Wellington, New Zealand.

== Selected works ==
* ''Towards a Warmer: What Climate Change Will Mean For New Zealand's Future World'', Meduna, V (2015), Wellington, New Zealand, Bridget Williams Books<ref>{{Cite book|title=Towards a warmer world : what climate change will mean for New Zealand's future|last=Veronika|first=Meduna|year=2015|isbn=9780908321735|location=Wellington, New Zealand|oclc=930367343}}</ref>
* ''Science on Ice: Discovering the Secrets of Antarctica,'' Meduna, V (2013), Auckland, New Zealand, Auckland University Press<ref>{{Cite book|title=Science on ice : discovering the secrets of Antarctica|last=Veronika.|first=Meduna|date=2012|publisher=Auckland University Press|isbn=9781869405830|location=Auckland, N.Z.|oclc=767879443}}</ref>
* ''Atoms, Dinosaurs and DNA: 68 Great New Zealand Scientists'', Meduna, V, Priestley, R (2008) Auckland, New Zealand, Random House<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C7ObMAAACAAJ|title=Atoms, Dinosaurs & DNA: 68 Great New Zealand Scientists|last1=Meduna|first1=Veronika|last2=Priestley|first2=Rebecca|date=2008|publisher=Random House New Zealand|isbn=9781869419547|language=en}}</ref>
